items.title: Illinois secures $68 million federal grant for Metra station accessibility upgrades

items.title: 1282 Washington: 75% Pre-Sold West Loop Condominium Development
items.summary: The WCA welcomes 1282 Washington, a ZSD development, as the headline sponsor of Madison Row Fest 2026. The building will deliver 4- and 5-bedroom single-family condominium residences, with 75% pre-sold and under construction, set to open next fall. The boutique building aims to set a new standard for West Loop living.

items.title: Inaugural West Loop Wellness Fest to Kick Off September 19

The event will feature local health and wellness businesses, instructor-led fitness and wellness classes, vendor experiences, and padel activities. A portion of ticket sales will benefit Mercy Home for Boys & Girls. Registration is required and space is limited.

items.title: Madison Row Fest Celebrates West Loop Community on September 12
items.summary: Madison Row Fest, a family-friendly community block party, will be held on Saturday, September 12 on Madison Street in the West Loop. The festival will include live entertainment, food and drinks, local vendors, kids' activities, and neighborhood traditions. The WCA is proud to welcome 1282 Washington as the headline sponsor of the event. The festival celebrates the best of the West Loop community.

items.title: LaSalle Central Small Business Improvement Fund Applications Open September 1
items.summary: The Department of Planning and Development’s Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF) will accept applications in the LaSalle Central TIF district starting September 1. SBIF offers reimbursement grant funding for permanent building improvements and repairs. An informational webinar is scheduled for 1 p.m. on Wednesday, September 2. Businesses can register online to learn more and apply.

items.title: Four New Historic Plaques to be Installed in West Loop this Summer

items.title: Business group pitches a 15-minute O'Hare-to-downtown train
items.summary: A group of business leaders behind a venture called the O'Hare Flyer wants to build a privately financed high-speed train linking O'Hare with a new depot near Van Buren and Canal streets in the South Loop, steps from Union Station. Trains would leave every 15 minutes and make the trip in about 15 minutes, with fares expected to fall between a $5 Blue Line ride and the cost of a cab or ride share. Backers put the cost at $2.25 billion and the timeline at up to five years, all privately financed, and Mayor Brandon Johnson said Tuesday he welcomes the idea. Unlike Elon Musk's abandoned 2018 tunnel plan, the Flyer would run on existing freight rail corridors instead of boring under the city.
